claim: On 50M Cohere 768-dim embeddings, Postgres with pgvector+pgvectorscale (StreamingDiskANN) achieved 28x lower p95 latency and 16x higher throughput than Pinecone s1 at 99% recall, at ~75% lower cost ($835 vs $3,241/mo).
quote: 28x lower p95 latency and 16x higher query throughput compared to Pinecone's storage optimized (s1) index for approximate nearest neighbor queries at 99% recall ... $835 ... $3,241

claim: pgvectorscale adds StreamingDiskANN (a disk-based index inspired by Microsoft DiskANN), Statistical Binary Quantization compression, and label-based filtered vector search via Microsoft Filtered DiskANN research.
quote: A new index type called StreamingDiskANN, inspired by the DiskANN algorithm ... Statistical Binary Quantization ... Label-based filtered vector search: based on Microsoft's Filtered DiskANN research

claim: Keeping vectors as a native Postgres column lets vector similarity combine with any SQL filter (WHERE, JOINs, full-text) and keeps relational and vector workloads transactionally consistent with full referential integrity, avoiding multi-system sync.
quote: your relational workload and vector workload are transactionally consistent with full referential integrity so you never get dangling records ... combine vector similarity search with any standard SQL filter: WHERE clauses, JOINs, full-text search

claim: 2026 throughput estimates: pgvector ~5K-15K QPS, Qdrant ~30K-80K QPS, Weaviate ~25K-50K QPS, Milvus 100K+ QPS at scale; guidance is pgvector if you have Postgres, Qdrant if not, Milvus only at very large scale.
quote: pgvector if you have Postgres, Qdrant if you do not. Reach for Milvus only at very large scale ... ~5K-15K QPS ... ~30K-80K QPS ... 100K+ QPS at scale

claim: For most SMB RAG under ~5M vectors pgvector is the correct default; reach for a dedicated store only at measurable limits, with Pinecone winning ease at 5M+, Qdrant fastest filtered search, Weaviate built-in hybrid search, Milvus at billion-vector scale.
quote: for most SMB RAG use cases under 5M vectors, pgvector is the correct default ... Pinecone wins at 5M+ vectors ... Qdrant if you need the absolute fastest filtered search ... Milvus if you're working at billion-vector scale

claim: At 100M-vector scale, monthly cost estimates put Qdrant on-disk HNSW at ~$600-900, Weaviate ~$700-1,000, Milvus ~$800-1,200, and Pinecone pods at $4,000-7,000+, making self-hosting economically justified at that scale.
quote: Qdrant self-hosted with on-disk HNSW (~$600-900/month ... Milvus on Kubernetes (~$800-1,200/month) ... Pinecone pods ($4,000-7,000+/month) ... Weaviate self-hosted cluster (~$700-1,000/month)

claim: GitHub stars (June 2026): pgvector/pgvector ~21.7K, timescale/pgvectorscale ~3.0K, qdrant/qdrant ~32.0K, weaviate/weaviate ~16.3K, milvus-io/milvus ~44.7K.
quote: Postgres extension for vector search (DiskANN), complements pgvector for performance and scale. Postgres OSS licensed.
